header.title: De natiuitate domini ſermo: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Alcuin
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:menota:alcuin:de-natiuitate-domini-ſermo:am-619-4to, from the Medieval Nordic Text Archive, Menota (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.

notes.17r.22: 17r.12 holds only a stop. 17r.14 writes 'spá sǫgum' / 'spá sǫgur' (prophecies) twice. líflyf qvenna, 'women's potions', is literally 'women's life-medicines', herbal charms.
notes.61r.17a: This passage is a miracle of St Olaf (a woman with a monthly seizure calls on Mary and Olaf), not part of the Christmas sermon under which it is filed.

nodes.text: you shall now hear: church-theft and robbery, manslaughter, long-held grudges
envy, pride, arrogance, whoredom, drunkenness, theft and all
injustice, looseness, perjury, bribes, and belief in women's potions
or sorceries,
or in prophecies. That is all the devil's craft, and
with it he lures most men away from
Christ and to hell. For
that reason we must guard against all of it, and against unseemliness and
excessive pride
carefully of her how
often that attack came upon her, or
whether any healing might be had
for her relief. She said too that the evil sickness, in
every month,
visited her, and no healing, medicine or spells, she said,
could be of help to her.
Now in the grief and misery which they
had suffered,
both of them, husband and wife, she called on the holy maiden Mary,
who certainly is
truly the mother of mercy, and on the holy Olaf
